## tsa-a02-v01 — argument map

**Speaker.** Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, promising)

**Question.** What comes first, and what is promised?

**Premises.**
- Now the means-less itself, first of all.
- We shall expound.

**Inference.** The means-less itself is announced first: exposition promised.

## tsa-a02-v02 — argument map

**Speaker.** Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, describing)

**Question.** Whose immersion needs no means?

**Premises.**
- Pierced by firm descent of power, discriminating of oneself, teacher's word heeded but once.
- Then: means-devoid, ever-risen — his immersion.

**Inference.** The struck one's immersion is means-devoid and ever-risen.

## tsa-a02-v03 (3)
Here / reason-itself-is-the-yoga-limb / thus / how / does-he-discriminate / If-asked / it-is-said / this / Lord / self-light-natured / own-self / Therein / what / is-done / by-means / Not-attainment-of-nature / from-eternity / not-notification / from-self-shiningness / not-removal-of-covering / since-covering-of-any-kind-is-impossible / not-entry-into-it / since-there-is-no-distinct-enterer // tsa02-p01
chunks.l2: Here "yoga-limb" means one thing only: thinking it through. But what is there to think? The Lord, who is self-shining, is yourself. So what could a means do? It can't get you your nature — you have it eternally. It can't inform you — you shine already. It can't strip a covering — there is none. It can't take you inside — there's no outsider to go in.

## tsa-a02-v03 — argument map

**Speaker.** Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, reasoning)

**Question.** What can means accomplish?

**Premises.**
- Reasoning itself is yoga's limb — but how discern at all?
- This Lord, self-light-natured, is own self: what could means do?
- No attaining of nature — eternal.
- No notifying — self-luminous manifestation needs none.
- No veil-removal — no covering of any kind exists.
- No entering the non-entered — enterer and entered not distinct.

**Inference.** Every use of means is void: nothing to attain, notify, unveil, or enter — all is Śiva already.

chunks.l2: And the means itself, as something separate from you, is equally impossible. So: all this is one reality, consciousness and nothing else — time can't measure it, place can't bound it, qualities can't fade it, shapes can't rule it, words can't point it out, proofs can't build it up. By its own will it is what lets everything from time to proof arrive at its nature; free, thick bliss; and that is I, with the universe mirrored inside me. Who sees this steadily is immersed in the Lord always, without means — no mantra binds him, no worship, no sitting, no observance.

## tsa-a02-v04 — argument map

**Speaker.** Abhinavagupta (teacher voice, concluding)

**Question.** Who am I, and what need of means?

**Premises.**
- What means here? Of it too, as distinct — impossible.
- Hence all this is one consciousness-only reality: unmeasured, unbounded, unfaded, uncontrolled, unindicated, unelaborated.
- By own will alone: autonomous, bliss-dense reality.
- That am I; therein, within me, the universe reflected.
- For one firmly discerning, ever: Lordly immersion, means-less itself.
- For it no constraint at all — by mantra, worship, meditation, conduct.

**Inference.** I am That; the universe mirrors in me; immersion is ever-present and means-less.
